subject: How do I make a stacked bar or stacked pie (polar coordinates) chart for following data?

messages.author: 4cf1dc5b0a7f2fd3
messages.subject: How do I make a stacked bar or stacked pie (polar coordinates) chart for following data?
parts:
I am new to R and ggplot2, but I have reviewed the following docs: http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/coord_polar.html and http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/geom_bar.html

Still, I don't know how to present the following data as stacked (or faceted) by village:
 var1= c(vil1, vil2, vil3, vil4) 
 var2 = c(16,11,2,1) 
 var3 = c(19,27,6,8) 
 var4 = c(7,11,14,9)
 var5= c(2,2,0,6)
 var6= c(24,29,23,44)
 var7= c(4,3,11,15)

Thanks!

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: How do I make a stacked bar or stacked pie (polar coordinates) chart for following data?
parts:
You want all your data in a single data frame, something like this:

d <- structure(list(var1 = structure(1:4, .Label = c("vil1", "vil2",
"vil3", "vil4"), class = "factor"), var2 = c(16, 11, 2, 1), var3 = c(19,
27, 6, 8), var4 = c(7, 11, 14, 9), var5 = c(2, 2, 0, 6), var6 = c(24,
29, 23, 44), var7 = c(4, 3, 11, 15)), .Names = c("var1", "var2",
"var3", "var4", "var5", "var6", "var7"), row.names = c(NA, -4L
), class = "data.frame")

print( d )
library(reshape)
d_melt <- melt( d, id.vars=1 )

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(d_melt,aes(var1,value,fill=variable))+geom_bar(stat="identity")

Regards,
Ben
